prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1159; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported in Houston, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just give the facts, if that's fine. I'm the driver of the blue sedan that was hit from behind.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?

A: I was stopped at a red light in the right lane, waiting to turn. I had been stopped for maybe ten or fifteen seconds when I felt the impact.

Q: Did you notice the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. I checked my mirror earlier, but I wasn't watching it closely. The first thing I registered was the noise and the jolt forward.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was. The belt locked up hard, and I think that's when my wrist got hurt. I put my right hand out to brace myself against the steering wheel.

Q: Where are you receiving treatment for the wrist?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same afternoon. They took X-rays and said it was fractured. I've been referred to an orthopedic doctor, and I have a follow-up appointment next week.

Q: Has anyone at the scene been injured besides yourself?

A: My passenger said her neck was sore, but she didn't go to a hospital. I don't know if she's seen anyone since.

Q: Did you give a statement to the police?

A: Yes, an officer came out and wrote a report. I gave him my account and I signed what he gave me.

Q: Is there anything you'd like to add that I haven't asked?

A: Just that I'm still having trouble gripping things with my right hand, and I'm worried about missing work. That's about it.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
